definition: Extracting clinical relations — drug-drug interactions, treatment-condition links — from biomedical text for pharmacovigilance and knowledge bases.
details: Extracting clinical relations — drug-drug interactions, treatment-condition links — from biomedical text for pharmacovigilance and knowledge bases.

explainer.lead: Medical relation extraction pulls clinical relations, such as drug-drug interactions and treatment-condition links, out of biomedical text. It matters for pharmacovigilance and for building knowledge bases.

tiers.eli5: It reads medical writing and picks out statements like 'this drug interacts with that one' so they can be collected automatically.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to biomedical literature to populate interaction records and knowledge bases. A pitfall is that missed interactions matter for safety monitoring, so recall is critical.
tiers.paperLevel: The task identifies relations between clinical entities in biomedical text; no formal formula or benchmark bound is given.

explainer.example: From a paper's text, the system extracts a link stating that a given drug interacts with another drug, logging it for safety review.
